headline.text: Youth-led protests sweep France and Germany
headline.context: Third weekend of cost-of-living marches in France.
headline.vo: Young people marched across Europe on Saturday, angry about living costs and run-down schools. It was France's third weekend of protests, and the movement has reached Germany.

beats.label: protesters in France, the government says
beats.vo: French authorities counted three hundred and twenty thousand protesters, fewer than two weeks ago. Organisers said nearly half a million. Hundreds of people were arrested, and police fired tear gas in Paris and Lyon.

In Germany, the youth group Gen Z regelt called rallies in more than thirty cities. Police in Cologne used water cannon, and in Frankfurt shop windows were smashed. In Lisbon, thousands marched peacefully over housing costs.

beats.quote: At my school, the ceiling is collapsing because of water damage.
beats.vo: The movement began with French students protesting teacher shortages and neglected buildings. A Berlin student told AP that at her school, the ceiling is collapsing. Similar youth-led protests have spread across Europe.

title: Youth-led protests over living costs sweep France and Germany
caption: Hundreds of thousands of mostly young people protested in France on Saturday, the third weekend of marches over living costs and school conditions, with hundreds arrested. The movement spread to more than 30 German cities, where police used water cannon in Cologne. Similar youth-led protests have been growing across Europe in recent weeks.
